messages.subject: BCV plot before calculateDiffMeth
parts:
Hi Altuna,

I am doing differential methylation analysis using methylKit. I am having difficulties in understanding the different results I am getting by changing the arguments in 'calculateDiffMeth' function, so I appreciate it if you could help.

I generated myDiff object, and filtered hypo and hyper CpG loci using the following code :

library(methylKit)

file.list=list('ALS1_792_hg19/ALS1_CG_report.txt',
               'ALS3_793_hg19/ALS3_CG_report.txt',
               'ALS4_794_hg19/ALS4_CG_report.txt',
               'ALS6_798_hg19/ALS6_CG_report.txt',
               'ALS7_797_hg19/ALS7_CG_report.txt',
               'ALS8_799_hg19/ALS8_CG_report.txt',
               'ACRI22_795_hg19/ACRI22_CG_report.txt',
               'ACRI247_796_hg19/ACRI247_CG_report.txt',
               'Prost018_791_hg19/Prost018_CG_report.txt'
)

myobj = methRead(location = file.list, sample.id = list("ALS1","ALS3","ALS4","ALS6", "ALS7", "ALS8", "ACRI22", "ACRI247", "Prost018"), 
                  assembly = "hg19", dbtype = "tabix", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                  header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t", resolution = "base", 
                  treatment = c(1,1,1,1,1,1,0,0,0), dbdir = "ALS_methyl_call", mincov = 10, )
meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L)
pm=percMethylation(meth.min)
mds=matrixStats::rowSds(pm)

myDiff=calculateDiffMeth(meth.min)

myDiff25p_hyper <- getMethylDiff(myDiff,difference=25,qvalue=0.01, type= "hyper")

Now, when I added covariates to my calculateDiffMeth there is a drastic decrease in CpG loci:

I am want to figure out how the number of CpGs changed so much? Overdispersion correction has drastically decreased them but I am not sure why this could have occurred?
I also wanted to plot the biological coefficient of variation (BCV) and not sure how to do that with my methylDiff object. I would highly appreciate it if you can help me understand the whole concept of overdispersion and its effect on false positives and how covariates have affected the analysis.

Thank you,
Shruti

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] BCV plot before calculateDiffMeth
parts:
Data is not like RNA-seq, I think the easiest thing could be to transform the percent methylation values as follows: log2((p.meth+1)/(100-p.meth+1))
This transformation will make the methylation values similar to a normal distribution, then you can calculate the coefficient of variation, which is standard deviation divided by mean. 

It is difficult to get the over-dispersion parameter out of the logistic regression model. If you just want the coefficient of variation, I suggest the method above. 

Best,
Altuna
